questions.question: Draw a cross-section of Earth and label the four layers: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
Use color or labels to show which layers are solid and which are liquid.
Show how the crust is different under the ocean and under a continent.
Sketch convection currents in the mantle. Use arrows to show where material rises and sinks.
Draw Earth's magnetic field. Label the layer that helps create it.
Draw a divergent boundary. Use arrows for plate movement and label what forms.
Draw an ocean plate meeting a continental plate. Label the trench and the volcanoes.
Draw two continental plates colliding. What landform forms?
Draw a transform boundary with arrows for plate movement. Add a star where earthquakes happen.
Draw an earthquake and label the focus and the epicenter.
Draw the water cycle. Label evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
Show where the energy for the water cycle comes from.
Add transpiration, runoff and groundwater to your water cycle.
Draw a mountain where one side gets lots of rain and the other side is dry. Explain with arrows.
Draw the rock cycle. Label igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rock and the processes that connect them.
Show how an igneous rock can become a sedimentary rock.
Draw layers of sedimentary rock. Label the oldest layer.
Draw where heat and pressure make metamorphic rock.
Sketch magma cooling slowly underground and quickly at the surface. Show the crystal sizes.
Draw a cold front from the side. Show the warm air, cold air and where storms form.
Draw a warm front from the side.
Draw a high pressure and a low pressure system. Use arrows for the wind.
Draw how air moves in a sea breeze on a sunny afternoon.
Draw a plant cell and label at least 5 organelles.
Draw an animal cell. Label the nucleus, cell membrane and mitochondria.
Draw two structures that only plant cells have.
Show a substance moving across the cell membrane by diffusion. Use arrows.
Draw a food chain with 4 organisms. Use arrows to show the flow of energy.
Draw a food web with at least 2 producers and 2 consumers.
Draw what happens to the web if the top predator is removed.
Draw an energy pyramid and show how much energy moves up each level.
Draw the particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas.
Show what happens to the particles when ice melts.
Draw the energy transformations on a roller coaster from the top of the first hill to the bottom.
Draw a light ray reflecting off a mirror. Label the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection.
Draw a simple circuit with a battery, a switch and a bulb.
Plot (2, 3), (4, 7) and (6, 11) and connect them. What is the slope?
Draw a number line from -5 to 5 and plot -3, 0.5 and 4.
Sketch a speed-vs-time graph of a car that speeds up, cruises, then stops.
Graph y = 2x + 1.
Draw fraction bars to model 3/4 + 1/2.
